entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h: MessagePack: Nested arrays can blow past buffer length limits
entry.content:
MessagePack: Nested arrays can blow past buffer length limits

Aliases: CVE-2026-92707

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • MessagePack — fixed in 2.5.303
  • MessagePack — fixed in 3.1.9

### Impact MessagePack-CSharp is vulnerable to denial of service through excessive memory allocation when deserializing attacker-controlled data into `System.Object`. When `PrimitiveObjectFormatter` encounters an array, it allocates an `object[]` using the declared array length **before** enforcing the configured maximum object-graph depth. A specially crafted payload containing deeply nested arrays can therefore keep many large arrays live simultaneously before deserialization is rejected for exceeding the depth limit. Because the array-header validation uses the total unread byte count as evidence that the declared elements may be present, nested array headers can reuse the same trailing bytes for this validation. This permits a relatively small payload to cause disproportionately lar…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-7pxr-59rr-hqj2: Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion
entry.content:
Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion

Aliases: CVE-2026-72923

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader — fixed in 3.10.0
  • Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader — fixed in 2.12.0
  • Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers — fixed in 1.6.30

### Impact A small YAML OpenAPI document containing nested anchors and aliases can cause uncontrolled resource consumption in Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers. The issue affects OpenAPI document parsing through the public YAML reader APIs and can cause the parsing process to allocate excessive memory and terminate through out-of-memory conditions. ## Affected versions ### Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader * `>= 2.0.0-preview.11, < 2.12.0` * `>= 3.0.0, < 3.10.0` ### Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers * `< 1.6.30` ### Patches * For the 1.X major version, versions 1.6.30 and above are patched. * For the 2.X major version, versions 2.12.0 and above are patched. * For the 3.X major version, versions 3.10.0 and above are patched. ## Impact Applications, CLIs, developer tool…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-m6wq-39m7-9xpp: Metalama allows local code execution through DLL planting in shared temporary directories
entry.content:
Metalama allows local code execution through DLL planting in shared temporary directories

Aliases: CVE-2026-62847

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:L/VI:H/VA:L/SC:L/SI:H/SA:H

Affected:

  • Metalama.Framework — fixed in 2026.1.19
  • Metalama.Tool — fixed in 2026.1.19
  • Metalama.Framework — fixed in 2025.1.18
  • Metalama.Tool — fixed in 2025.1.18
  • Metalama.Tool — fixed in 2026.0.25
  • Metalama.Framework — fixed in 2026.0.25

## Summary Metalama loaded and executed compile-time assemblies, auxiliary executable tools, and embedded helper assemblies from predictable temporary directories. On Linux and macOS the default cache location was the world-writable system temporary directory (`Path.GetTempPath()`, i.e. `/tmp`), and previously-generated artifacts were trusted based on the presence of a sentinel/`.completed` marker file rather than on any integrity verification. A local, unprivileged user on a shared machine or CI/build agent can pre-create the deterministic cache directory structure and plant a malicious DLL together with the matching sentinel file. When a higher-privileged user (or build/service account) subsequently runs a build, Metalama finds the sentinel, skips regeneration, and loads and executes t…
